narrative: Fire and climate dominate today's feed: a Global Change Biology review frames the global fire crisis as compounding human and bioclimatic drivers, while work on post-fire nitrogen banks asks whether boreal conifer recovery relies on subsurface stocks. Climate-response papers show Europe's mountain flora facing compositional turnover, drought metrics biasing estimates of ecosystem water limitation, and migratory waterfowl tracking vegetation green-up better when they use more stopovers. In movement and behaviour, GPS data from 586 mammals show human presence rather than buildings drives avoidance during lockdowns, and female bears use human subsidies while managing risk spatially. Population studies find kangaroo reproductive drivers often fail to scale up to recruitment. Community and landscape work highlights newly planted woodlands improving connectivity, and elephants reshaping rather than degrading rainforest bird communities. On methods, new tools include an R package for camera traps, a passive acoustic workflow, Bacpipe for bioacoustic deep learning, and LiDAR-based tree morphometrics, alongside a reinforcement-learning model for restoration planning.
